items.entity: fixed support of the cantilever (presumably the left edge)
items.description: Sec. 4.1 never states the supports. It only calls the problem a 'classic 2D cantilever beam' and later mentions 'members near the fixed-boundary corners'. The boundary sketch is only in the Fig. 3 'problem setup (bottom left)' panel. The left edge is implied only because the load is on the right edge.
readings: Entire left edge x = 0 (0 <= y <= 100 mm, all 101 nodes) fixed
Only the central part of the left edge fixed (e.g., middle 50% of the height)
Only short segments at the top-left and bottom-left corners fixed

items.entity: constrained DOFs on the left-edge support
items.description: Sec. 4.1 does not say which displacement components are fixed. Sec. 4.3 says 'fully clamped', but only for its own clamped-clamped problem. 'Fixed-boundary' in Sec. 4.1 suggests clamping, but the actual condition is shown only in Fig. 3.
readings: Clamped: u_x = u_y = 0 at every support node
Roller: u_x = 0 along the edge, with u_y fixed at a single node only (e.g., mid-height)

items.entity: 100 MPa traction on the right edge - location along the edge
items.description: Sec. 4.1 says the traction is applied 'to the right edge of the beam', which reads naturally as the whole edge. Sec. 4.4 explicitly returns to the Sec. 4.1 cantilever and says 'with the traction applied at the center of the right edge'.
readings: Centered at mid-height of the right edge (x = 200 mm, y = 50 mm, i.e., 0.5 H)
Spread uniformly over the full right edge (y = 0 to 1.0 H)

items.entity: length and nodal distribution of the loaded segment on the right edge
items.description: Neither Sec. 4.1 nor Sec. 4.4 gives the length of the traction patch; only its intensity (100 MPa) is stated. The text also doesn't say whether the load is integrated as a consistent traction or lumped at nodes. Only Fig. 3 might show it.
readings: Single nodal point force at (200, 50) mm
One element edge (1 mm) adjacent to mid-height
2 mm segment, y = 49-51 mm, uniform
10 mm segment, y = 45-55 mm (0.1 H), uniform
20 mm segment, y = 40-60 mm (0.2 H), uniform
Full 100 mm right edge, uniform

items.entity: 100 MPa traction on the right edge - direction
items.description: Sec. 4.1 and Sec. 4.4 give only 'a 100 MPa traction' with no direction. Only Sec. 4.3, a different problem, says 'downward'. A cantilever bending load is implied, but the arrow appears only in the Fig. 3 setup panel.
readings: Vertical downward (-y), i.e., shear/tangential to the right edge
Vertical upward (+y)
Horizontal outward normal (+x, tension)

items.entity: resultant force of the right-edge traction
items.description: Only the traction intensity (100 MPa, Sec. 4.1) and the 1 mm thickness (Sec. 4 defaults) are given. The resultant force a compliance solver needs is 100 MPa x loaded length x 1 mm, so it depends on the unspecified patch length.
readings: 100 N (1 mm tributary length / point load)
200 N (2 mm patch)
1,000 N (10 mm patch)
2,000 N (20 mm patch)
10,000 N (full 100 mm edge)

items.description: The starting design for the 2D examples is never given. The Sec. 4 defaults list only mesh, MMA, time integration and material; an initial field is stated only for the 3D blade (Sec. 4.5). Sec. 4.3 says the problem is non-convex, so the starting design can change the result.
readings: Uniform rho = V* = 0.5
Uniform rho = 1.0
Uniform 0.5 with a small random perturbation

items.entity: density field entering the V* = 0.5 constraint
items.description: Eq. 19 writes the volume constraint with rho, the raw design variable. Sec. 3.2, however, calls the filtered rho-tilde the physical density used in the FEA. The text never says explicitly which field is constrained; with the density filter, the two averages differ near the domain boundary.
readings: Mean of raw design variables rho <= 0.5 (literal Eq. 19)
Mean of filtered densities rho-tilde <= 0.5

items.entity: MMA objective scaling and internal constants
items.description: Sec. 3.4 and Sec. 4 use the Deetman (2025) MMA 'with default parameters' and a 0.1 move limit. The text doesn't say whether J_el = f^T u_0 is normalized, and it doesn't list the MMA constants. Sec. 4.3 itself attributes topology differences to 'MMA sensitivity to objective magnitude'.
readings: Unnormalized J_el (N*mm) with the library's default MMA constants
J_el normalized by its value at the initial design
J_el scaled to a fixed value (e.g., 100) at the first iteration

items.description: Sec. 3.5 says the loop stops 'when the design and objective change fall below a prescribed tolerance'. Sec. 4 says it stops after 250 iterations or when max|rho_i - rho_(i-1)| <= 1e-5, with no objective criterion. The objective tolerance is never given.
readings: Stop at 250 iterations or max|delta rho| <= 1e-5 (design change only)
Also stop when the relative objective change falls below an unstated tolerance (e.g., 1e-4)

items.entity: non-design (forced solid/void) regions, e.g., around the load patch
items.description: Sec. 4.1 doesn't mention passive or non-design elements at all, and the setup sketch is only in Fig. 3. With a concentrated 100 MPa traction it is unclear whether the elements under the loaded segment are forced solid.
readings: None: all 200 x 100 elements are design variables
A solid (rho = 1) non-design pad of a few elements beneath the loaded segment of the right edge

locator: Sec. 4.1, the structural cantilever baseline design minimizing elastic compliance (Fig. 3)
